one of the three who forbid in the Kutim baraita (24a.1)
the 23a.7 baraita: animal as a sukkah wall; re-cited דתניא at 24a.2
the mishnah cited והתנן at 23b.2: the wife of an absent kohen eats teruma
the mishnah cited ורמינן עלה at 23b.3: a get effective an hour before death
the דתניא at 23b.5-24a.1, wine bought from Kutim, with its seifa quoted at 24a.6
the אמרו לו of the Kutim baraita's seifa (24a.6); re-identified at 24a.7 as R' Yehuda
the mishnah cited והא תנן at 24a.8 (R' Yehuda: another wife is prepared for the High Priest)
the mishnah cited אלמה תנן at 24a.9: R' Yehuda -- impure as golel, R' Meir -- pure
first version of Rav Acha bar Yaakov's statement (24a.10)
the איכא דאמרי version of Rav Acha bar Yaakov's statement (24a.10)

props.gloss_en: the baraita: one who makes his sukkah atop an animal -- R' Meir validates (encoded at its home in sukkah_23a_al_gabei_behema)
the stam: and R' Meir -- this one too is fit by Torah law [for the seven days]; it is the Sages who decreed against [using] it
if one made an animal a wall for a sukkah -- R' Meir invalidates
and R' Yehuda validates
R' Meir: anything with the breath of life may be made neither a sukkah wall, nor an alley side-post, nor a well-board, nor a grave-cover
in R' Yosei HaGelili's name they said: nor may women's bills of divorce be written on it (same content as sukkah_24b_sefer_keritut's p_ryhg_ein_kotvin, where the אמר מר takes it up)
Abaye: R' Meir's reason is lest the animal die
R' Zeira: R' Meir's reason is lest it flee

the stam, first round: a tied elephant -- all agree [it is valid], for even dead its carcass is ten [tefachim]; they differ on an untied elephant -- on lest-die we are not concerned, on lest-flee we are
the stam, second round: an untied elephant -- all agree [it is invalid]; they differ on a tied animal -- on lest-die we are concerned, on lest-flee we are not
the stam, for the lest-flee view: death is not common
an Israelite woman married to a kohen whose husband went overseas eats teruma, on the presumption that he is alive
[a kohen who says] 'this is your get an hour before my death' -- she is forbidden to eat teruma at once
Abaye: the presumption-of-life mishnah is R' Meir's
Abaye: the an-hour-before-my-death mishnah is R' Yehuda's
Abaye: R' Meir is not concerned for [possible] death
Abaye: R' Yehuda is concerned for [possible] death
one who buys wine from the Kutim says: two log I will separate are teruma, ten first tithe, nine second tithe; he redeems [the second tithe] and drinks at once -- R' Meir
R' Yehuda, R' Yosei and R' Shimon forbid [drinking before separation]
the baraita's seifa: they said to R' Meir -- do you not concede that perhaps the wineskin will burst, and he will turn out retroactively to have drunk untithed produce?
R' Meir answered them: when it bursts [then we will be concerned]
the stam, reversing: R' Meir IS concerned for death
the stam, reversing: and R' Yehuda is NOT concerned for death
the stam, speaking for R' Meir: death is common
the stam, speaking for R' Meir: a burst wineskin is not common -- he can hand it to a watchman
the stam: R' Yehuda's reason [for forbidding the Kutim wine] is not concern for a burst wineskin but that he does not hold bereira
there it is R' Yehuda who says to R' Meir: for me, there is no bereira
the Yoma mishnah: R' Yehuda says -- they even prepare another wife for him [the High Priest], lest his wife die
Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua: they made a higher standard for atonement
the stam: on both the lest-die and the lest-flee view, it is a proper partition by Torah law, and it is the Sages who decreed against it
the mishnah: R' Yehuda -- [a living creature as grave-cover] imparts impurity as a golel
the mishnah: and R' Meir deems it pure
Rav Acha bar Yaakov: R' Meir holds that any partition that stands by air [breath] is no partition
some say Rav Acha bar Yaakov said: R' Meir holds that any partition not made by human hands is no partition
the stam: what is between them? a partition made of an inflated wineskin
on the version 'stands by air is no partition': it stands by air [so it is no partition]
on the version 'not made by human hands is no partition': it is made by human hands [so it is a partition]

supports.gloss_en: ורבי מאיר, הא נמי מדאורייתא מחזא חזיא -- on R' Meir's view the sukkah atop an animal IS fit for seven days by Torah law; only a rabbinic decree bars using it
שהיה רבי מאיר אומר: כל דבר שיש בו רוח חיים אין עושין אותו לא דופן לסוכה... -- the baraita grounds R' Meir's psul in his general rule

דתניא: R' Meir lets the buyer of Kutim wine drink at once on the strength of a future separation; R' Yehuda, R' Yosei and R' Shimon forbid -- the baraita adduced for Abaye's mapping (kind tanya_kevatei: no kind names a bare דתניא)
איפוך ... דתניא: עשאה לבהמה דופן לסוכה, רבי מאיר פוסל ורבי יהודה מכשיר -- the animal-wall baraita adduced for the reversal

objections.gloss_en: למאן דאמר גזרה שמא תמות, ניחוש שמא תברח! -- the lest-die view should also fear flight, so an untied elephant would be invalid on both views; unanswered, the stam restates the difference (אלא)
ומאן דאמר גזרה שמא תברח, ניחוש שמא תמות? -- why does the lest-flee view not fear death in the tied animal?

answered_by.gloss_en: מיתה לא שכיחא -- death is not common (= p_mita_lo_shechicha, aliba r_zeira)

objections.gloss_en: והאיכא רווחא דביני ביני? -- but there is the gap between [its legs]: how is the tied animal a wall at all?

answered_by.gloss_en: דעביד ליה בהוצא ודפנא -- he fills it with palm-leaves and laurel

objections.gloss_en: ודלמא רבעה? -- [on the lest-flee view] perhaps the tied animal will crouch [and the wall fall below ten]?

answered_by.gloss_en: דמתיחה באשלי מלעיל -- it is held taut by ropes from above

objections.gloss_en: ולמאן דאמר גזרה שמא תמות נמי, הא מתיחה באשלי מלעיל! -- if it is held by ropes from above, even dead it stays a wall: why does the lest-die view fear death?

answered_by.gloss_en: זמנין דמוקים בפחות משלשה סמוך לסכך, וכיון דמייתא כווצא ולאו אדעתיה -- sometimes it is set within three [tefachim] of the sekhakh, and once dead it shrinks and he does not notice

objections.gloss_en: ורמינן עלה: הרי זה גיטיך שעה אחת קודם מיתתי -- אסורה לאכול בתרומה מיד -- here we DO fear his death

answered_by.gloss_en: לא קשיא: הא רבי מאיר דלא חייש למיתה, הא רבי יהודה דחייש למיתה (= p_abaye_kayam_rm, p_abaye_mitati_ry)

objections.gloss_en: ומי אמר אביי רבי מאיר חייש למיתה ורבי יהודה לא חייש? -- yet Abaye himself resolved the Gittin mishnayot by saying R' Meir does NOT fear death and R' Yehuda does (kind svara under protest: no kind for an amoraic-memra contradiction)

answered_by.gloss_en: איפוך: רבי מאיר חייש למיתה ורבי יהודה לא חייש -- reverse [the Gittin mapping], as the animal-wall baraita shows (= p_rm_chayesh_lemita, p_ry_lo_chayesh_lemita)

objections.gloss_en: קשיא דרבי מאיר אדרבי מאיר! -- R' Meir fears death [the animal wall] yet does not fear a burst wineskin [the Kutim wine]

answered_by.gloss_en: אמר לך רבי מאיר: מיתה שכיחא, בקיעת הנוד לא שכיחא, אפשר דמסר ליה לשומר (= p_mita_shechicha, p_bekia_lo_shechicha, aliba r_meir)

objections.gloss_en: קשיא דרבי יהודה אדרבי יהודה! -- R' Yehuda does not fear death [the animal wall] yet forbids the Kutim wine

answered_by.gloss_en: טעמא דרבי יהודה לאו משום דחייש לבקיעת נוד, אלא משום דלית ליה ברירה (= p_ry_ein_breira)

objections.gloss_en: ולא חייש רבי יהודה לבקיעת נוד? והא מדקתני סיפא: אמרו לו לרבי מאיר: אי אתה מודה שמא יבקע הנוד...? ואמר להו: לכשיבקע. מכלל דחייש רבי יהודה לבקיעת הנוד!

answered_by.gloss_en: התם רבי יהודה הוא דקאמר לרבי מאיר: לדידי לית לי ברירה, אלא לדידך דיש ברירה -- אי אתה מודה דשמא יבקע הנוד? אמר ליה: לכשיבקע -- the concern was put to R' Meir within his own premise (= p_ry_lidi_ein_breira; the query aliba r_meir)

objections.gloss_en: ולא חייש רבי יהודה למיתה? והא תנן: רבי יהודה אומר אף אשה אחרת מתקינין לו, שמא תמות אשתו

answered_by.gloss_en: הא איתמר עלה, אמר רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: מעלה עשו בכפרה (= p_maalah_bekapara)

objections.gloss_en: אלא מעתה, לרבי מאיר תטמא משום גולל? אלמה תנן: רבי יהודה מטמא משום גולל ורבי מאיר מטהר -- if the animal were a proper partition by Torah law, R' Meir should make it impure as a grave-cover; unanswered (אלא אמר רב אחא בר יעקב follows)
